steward.comment: Began awkwardly and as a result was slow into stride. When questioned regarding her riding of Ultra Blue, apprentice Jade Smith, with the assistance of RV apprentice jockey coach, Darren Gauci, explained she had been instructed to lead at a comfortable tempo and not to restrain the gelding as it can have a tendency to race keenly when being restrained. J. Smith added after beginning only fairly, she urged her mount along in the early stages to obtain the lead passing the 1400m. J. Smith stated after passing the 1200m she glanced to her right where she was able to see Princeofnottingham and at this stage she was happy with the way Ultra Blue was travelling, however from this point was unaware of the margin she had commenced to establish over the remainder of the field. J. Smith added she placed the gelding under pressure from the 500m where she felt it responded before weakening over the final 200m and in her opinion, Ultra Blue may be better suited on turf tracks. J. Smith agreed with Stewards that she set too quick of a tempo from the 1200m and should have made a greater effort to ease her mount to allow it some respite in order to finish off the race strongly. Trainer representative Dara O'Meachair confirmed the nature of the instructions and reiterated that Ultra Blue had a tendency to race keenly and can resent being restrained, however he did not anticipate Ultra Blue leading by such a large margin. J. Smith was advised that her ride would be referred to the Racing Victoria Riders Skills Panel for review. A post-race veterinary examination did not reveal any significant findings.
